kp.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Arc Length of a Parametric Curve

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
![](images/ac/ac040bc2c3eb943f947f34602c7c03e90f18e129a0fa7749d8ae60faaab12f71.png)

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\pi ].
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

According to the double-angle formula for cosine, $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .$ Substituting $\theta =\frac{t}{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{t}{2}) & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ 2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =4{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\text{d}t \\  & =-2\cdot 2\cdot {\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-4(\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-4(0-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/51/5117030d23370b2167513b7a2eee5258aae4eb9f45ad428fd82e4334c4ce6638.png)

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=1+3t,\,y=2{t}^{3/2},\,t\in [0,1].
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+3t)=3\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3/2})=3{t}^{1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{(3{t}^{1/2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{9+9t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}(1+t)^{1/2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =3\cdot {\frac{2}{3}(1+t)^{3/2}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\sqrt{8}-2 \\  & =4\sqrt{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/da/da529910e268ea4c124d7c27b085ca1799e255604459c539cc8d5809dda8f95a.png)

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x={sin}^{3}⁡t,\,y={cos}^{3}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{3}⁡t)=3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{3}⁡t)=-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{(3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{9{sin}^{4}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{4}⁡t{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}(-1-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2{cos}^{3}⁡t,\,y=2{sin}^{3}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{cos}^{3}⁡t)=-6{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{sin}^{3}⁡t)=6{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{(-6{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(6{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{36{cos}^{4}⁡t{sin}^{2}⁡t+36{sin}^{4}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{36{sin}^{2}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(-1-1) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,y=2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,t\in [0,\pi ].
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{(2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4{t}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }t\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\cdot {\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =2(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}-0) \\  & ={\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,t\in [0,\pi ].
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t-8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+4{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+4{cos}^{2}⁡t-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4+4-8(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

According to the double-angle formula for cosine, $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .$ Substituting $\theta =\frac{t}{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{t}{2}) & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ 8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =16{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8{\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-8(\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-8(0-1) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=4\operatorname{sin}⁡t+5,\,y=4(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1),\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡t+5))=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1))=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(t).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}+(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(t))^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{16{cos}^{2}⁡(t)+16{sin}^{2}⁡(t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4t{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =4(\frac{\pi }{2}-0) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Find the arc length $L$ of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\pi ].
$$

Do not round the answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t-(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{t}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\end{aligned}

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =t\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\sqrt{{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\sqrt{{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\sqrt{{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\sqrt{{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{(2\pi )^{2}}{2}-0 \\  & =2{\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
x=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2,\,y=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-4,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{3}].
$$

Do not round the answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2) \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-4) \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{9}\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\text{d}t \\  & =3t\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =3(\frac{\pi }{3}-0) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Find the arc length of the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3,\,y=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1,\,t\in [\frac{\pi }{5},\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$

Do not round the answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3) \\  & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1) \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /5}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /5}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{25{cos}^{2}⁡t+25{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /5}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{25({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /5}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{25}\,\text{d}t \\  & =5{\int }_{\pi /5}^{\pi /2}\text{d}t \\  & =5t\,{|}_{\pi /5}^{\pi /2} \\  & =5(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{5}) \\  & =5\left(\frac{3\pi }{10}\right) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}) \\  & =t,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{3}(2t+1)^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2}(2t+1)^{1/2}\cdot 2 \\  & =(2t+1)^{1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\sqrt{(t)^{2}+{((2t+1)^{1/2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\sqrt{(t+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}|t+1|\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}+t)\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{4}{2}+2)-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}

and

To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$

$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)) \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) \\  & =3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))}^{2}+{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t-18\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+9{sin}^{2}⁡(3t)+9{cos}^{2}⁡t-18\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+9{cos}^{2}⁡(3t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{9+9-18(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t-t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

According to the double-angle formula for cosine, $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡t.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡(t) \\ 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & =2{sin}^{2}⁡(t) \\ 18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & =36{sin}^{2}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{18-18\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{36{sin}^{2}⁡(t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }|\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)|\,\text{d}t \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-6(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-6(-1-1) \\  & =12.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2t)=2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-1)\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{(2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-1))}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t+4{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

According to the double-angle formula for cosine, $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .$ Substituting $\theta =\frac{t}{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{t}{2}) & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =2{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \\ 8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t & =16{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\text{d}t \\  & =-2\cdot 4\cdot {\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-8(\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-8(0-1) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
